hints: For a given route, when can you walk it? Only once the water covers its highest cell. So which route has the smallest 'highest cell'?

Dijkstra with a min-heap where a route's cost is the maximum height along it, not the sum. Always expand the reachable cell with the lowest such cost; the first time the corner is popped gives the answer.

1. Push (grid[0][0], 0, 0) into a min-heap; mark it seen.
  2. Pop the smallest (t, x, y); if it is the bottom-right, return t.
  3. For each unseen neighbour, push (max(t, its height), neighbour) and mark it seen.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every t from 0 upwards and check with BFS whether the corners are connected using cells ≤ t.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: Binary search on t with a BFS check each time.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Dijkstra-style search on max-height cost with a heap.

explain: For [[0,1,2],[7,8,3],[6,5,4]], the heap starts with 0, then pops 1, 2, 3, 4 (each pushed as max(previous, height)) while the 7 and 8 cells wait at the bottom of the heap. When (2,2) with height 4 is popped, the answer is 4. Marking cells when pushing is safe here because heights are distinct and the cost only grows through max. A 1×1 grid answers its own height.
recognize: Minimise the worst (maximum) value along a path → Dijkstra with max instead of sum (a bottleneck path).
